title: Google Solution Challenge 2026
description: Build a technical solution for one of the 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals using Google technologies like Flutter, Firebase, GCP, Android, and Gemini AI.
overview: The Google Solution Challenge is an annual international technical competition inviting university students worldwide to solve local community problems aligned with the United Nations 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Participants leverage Google Cloud Platform, Flutter, Firebase, Android, and TensorFlow to architect production-ready software solutions while receiving direct technical mentorship from Google software engineers.

rounds.title: Round 1: Solution Ideation & Prototype Submission
rounds.description: Form a team of up to 4 students, choose 1 or more UN SDGs, and build a functioning application using Google developer tools. Submit a 2-minute video walkthrough showcasing user flow, system architecture, and public GitHub repository link.

rounds.title: Round 2: Top 50 Global Mentorship Cohort
rounds.description: The Top 50 global teams undergo deep technical reviews and receive weekly 1-on-1 mentorship sessions with Google software engineers to refine code quality, accessibility, cloud scalability, and UI/UX design.

rounds.title: Round 3: Global Final Demo Day & Live Pitch
rounds.description: Top 10 finalist teams present live virtually to Google Vice Presidents, Developer Relations Leaders, and UN Impact Directors to determine the Top 3 global winners.

eligibility: Must be an active student enrolled in an undergraduate or postgraduate degree program at an accredited college or university.
Teams must consist of 1 to 4 students (inter-college and inter-disciplinary teams are permitted).
Solutions must incorporate at least one core Google technology (Flutter, Firebase, GCP, Android, TensorFlow, Gemini AI).
Project must target at least one of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals.

prizes.reward: $3,000 USD per team member + 1-on-1 executive mentorship + Feature on official Google Developers Blog
$1,000 USD per team member + Custom Google Swag Package + Certificate of Distinction
Exclusive Google Cloud Swag Box + 1-on-1 Googler Technical Mentorship + Certificate of Achievement

faqs.question: Do all team members need to belong to the same GDSC chapter or university?
faqs.answer: No! Students from different universities, GDSC chapters, or degree streams can form a joint team as long as all members are active college students.

faqs.question: What qualifies as a Google technology for the submission?
faqs.answer: Any core Google platform qualifies, including Flutter, Firebase, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Android SDK, TensorFlow, ARCore, or Google Gemini AI APIs.

faqs.question: How are projects evaluated during Round 1?
faqs.answer: Projects are evaluated 50% on impact (how effectively it addresses the chosen UN SDG and solves a real community problem) and 50% on technology (effective use of Google tools, code quality, UI usability).
